gen_risks.description: Multi-party historical precedent and fragmented ministerial governance could cause weak inter-ministerial policy planning, monitoring, and coordination, impairing implementation of cross-sectoral competitiveness and jobs reforms.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish an inter-ministerial Policy Planning, Monitoring, and Coordination Working Group led by the Public Policy Secretariat with clear mandates, monitoring protocols, and semi-annual progress review mechanisms.
gen_risks.evidence: According to the Bank’s 2015 Systematic Country Diagnostic, policy coordination is among the weakest points for Serbia.

gen_risks.description: Lack of World Bank procurement experience in PPS, MoE, and MoLEVSA may result in procurement delays, errors, or non-compliance with Bank procedures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit experienced procurement experts within PPS and MoLEVSA prior to project implementation and conduct intensive procurement training and implementation support.
gen_risks.evidence: most of the entities involved in project implementation, have no experience in implementing World Bank-funded projects and with Bank procurement, except for MoESTD.

gen_risks.description: Political interference in subsidy allocation and overlapping agency mandates among SIEPA, Development Fund, AOFI, and NARR could derail restructuring of Ministry of Economy investment and export support programs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Formulate and officially adopt a transparent, strategic framework and costed action plan for agency restructuring, underpinned by strengthened governance and performance targets.
gen_risks.evidence: politics tend to interfere in making decisions on what programs to support... agencies have overlapping mandates, no coordination between them

gen_risks.description: Sub-projects and technology development supported under the Innovation Fund's Mini and Matching Grant Programs may trigger minor adverse environmental impacts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement the Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF), engage an independent environmental expert, and enforce Category A exclusion and EMP requirements for all grants.
gen_risks.evidence: Direct, physical environmental impacts could arise under Component 2 on Innovation, which includes DLIs supporting startups and enterprises

gen_risks.description: Excessive and highly uneven caseloads per caseworker across NES branch offices (ranging from 200 to over 2,000) threaten the quality of labor intermediation and employer outreach.
gen_risks.mitigation: Introduce a separate registry for temporarily inactive jobseekers, implement caseworker certification, and adopt a staffing plan to reallocate personnel and narrow caseload dispersion.
gen_risks.evidence: Currently, the average caseload varies between around 200 to over 2,000 registered unemployed per case worker across branch offices

gen_risks.description: High tax wedges on low-wage jobs and a 1-to-1 benefit reduction rule for social financial assistance recipients create strong disincentives to transition into formal work.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct analytical design studies and pilot an in-work cash transfer program for social assistance beneficiaries to partially reimburse lost benefits and lower effective tax rates.
gen_risks.evidence: Serbia has one of the highest tax wedges on low-paying jobs in the entire ECA Region and a social assistance benefit that is reduced

gen_risks.description: Public research institutes may resist public R&D sector reforms due to an academic culture that prioritizes publication volume over commercialization and IP protection.
gen_risks.mitigation: Perform comprehensive RDI self-assessments and international expert audits to inform a new Research & Innovation Strategy and performance-based financing schemes.
gen_risks.evidence: there exists a very strong academic culture, fueled by an incentive system that places a clear premium on publications with little incentives for protection

gen_risks.description: Civil service salary reductions and hiring freezes may constrain NES and ministry capacity to recruit and retain qualified caseworkers and technical personnel.
gen_risks.mitigation: Use project technical assistance funds for essential external expertise and reassign existing internal administrative personnel to frontline caseworker roles.
gen_risks.evidence: The recent reduction in civil service salaries, the ongoing constraints in the civil service to hire new workers, and budget limitation

gen_risks.description: Complex clearance and consultation requirements between PPS and line ministries could cause operational delays in procuring technical assistance consultancies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish clear timeline targets for Terms of Reference finalization, conduct close Bank monitoring, and utilize regular joint coordination meetings.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential procurement delays: arrangements for clearance of evaluation reports by the PPS may lead to procurement delays due to consultation with the respective implementing institutions;

gen_risks.description: Macroeconomic instability or external economic shocks (such as natural disasters) could impair fiscal consolidation efforts and disrupt government counterpart funding for project EEPs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Anchor macro-fiscal reforms within the 3-year IMF Precautionary Stand-By Agreement and utilize results-based IBRD reimbursements against essential salary budget lines.
gen_risks.evidence: The disastrous floods of May 2014 triggered a further recession... public debt to GDP ratio sharply increased

gen_risks.description: Lack of systematic cost-benefit analysis and impact evaluations in Ministry of Economy development agencies risks continued inefficient spending of public resources on state support programs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a specialized M&E center within MoE to establish performance targets, conduct cost-benefit analyses, and regularly evaluate support program outcomes.
gen_risks.evidence: Cost benefit analysis of existing support programs is currently not carried out in a systematic way by the MoE development agencies

gen_risks.description: Delays or failures in satisfying Disbursement-Linked Indicators (DLIs) could lead to withheld loan disbursements and financing gaps for Eligible Expenditure Programs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Structure DLIs to allow partial payments for mid-year progress, closely track DLI milestones via the PPMC Working Group, and provide targeted TA for reform achievement.
gen_risks.evidence: In the event a DLI is not achieved... Bank can issue a waiver and determine the amount and timing of the withheld disbursement

gen_risks.description: Uneven implementation of Financial Management and Control (FMC) standards across government bodies could lead to accounting or reporting inconsistencies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Assign dedicated FM personnel within the PPS PIU to consolidate semi-annual budget execution reports and submit independent annual project audits by acceptable audit firms.
gen_risks.evidence: Financial Management and Control (FMC), as designed by the Public Internal Financial Control (PIFC) framework... is not widely established and implemented across the government.

gt_risks.description: Program success relies on continuous, engaged commitment from the Prime Minister, Deputy PM, Minister of Finance, Minister of Education/Science/Technological Development, Minister of Labor/Employment/Veterans/Social Affairs, and the Public Policy Secretariat (PPS); line ministries must sustain interest in policy coordination or the loan will not disburse. Risk is heightened by political instability, frequent historical changes in ministers/senior staff, and excessive concentration of decision-making at the top (per the Bank's Systematic Country Diagnostic).
gt_risks.mitigation: Strong communications with the public, private sector, civil society, and EU Delegation to maintain a broad-based reform coalition; Bank coordinates communications with the PM's office; periodic PPMC Working Group consultations with private sector/civil society; ongoing close consultation with the EU Delegation in Serbia.

gt_risks.description: Significant downside macroeconomic risks: lower-than-expected Eurozone recovery could hurt Serbia's exports, remittances, and capital flows (EU countries are its largest trading partners). Materializing fiscal risks (e.g. SOE subsidy reduction difficulties) or weakening growth/currency would require even greater fiscal consolidation in 2015-2016 to keep public debt sustainable; reduced exports/FDI or greater consolidation could dampen anticipated reform impact.
gt_risks.mitigation: Bank works closely with government and the IMF to keep SOE/public-utility reform on track and ensure it generates required fiscal savings.

gt_risks.description: Project works across three ministries (MoE plus development agencies, MoESTD, MoLEVSA) plus the PPS, creating implementation complexity for both government and Bank. Achieving the DLIs requires substantial external technical assistance, but Bank supervision resources are limited and the government is reluctant to borrow for TA (would rather minimize loan-funded TA or substitute other donor resources), risking inadequate TA resourcing.
gt_risks.mitigation: Team seeks complementary resources (e.g. CIIP Trust Fund) and leverages work from other WBG projects; collaborates with other donors such as the EU and USAID.

gt_risks.description: Overall coordination sits with the Public Policy Secretariat (PPS), created only in spring 2014 under the new government; as a new institution it lacks capacity and a full set of official administrative procedures for cross-ministry policy coordination. Substantial risk to both project implementation (fiduciary/safeguards requirements, cross-ministry results reporting) and coordination of the inter-ministerial PPMC Working Group.
gt_risks.mitigation: PPS expected to hire additional personnel for fiduciary requirements and project coordination; Bank provides TA through the CIIP trust fund to strengthen PPS capacity.

gt_risks.description: PPS currently has no fiduciary experience managing Bank projects.
gt_risks.mitigation: Build capacity by establishing a Project Implementation Unit (PIU) within the PPS responsible for implementation, adequately staffing its fiduciary functions.

gt_risks.description: Reforms create both winners and losers, and losers are often more visible and organized at the time of reform (e.g. beneficiaries of MoE incentives/subsidies, National Employment Service case-workers, researchers at research institutes slated for restructuring).
gt_risks.mitigation: Government to clearly communicate reform objectives, expected outcomes, and benefits throughout the process.
